extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO enforcement staff, and legal community
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for imposing and carrying out reciprocal discipline against a patent practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including required notices, scope of suspension, and post-suspension obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's reciprocal discipline is predicated on his violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), having been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director filed a Complaint requesting reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the state court. Action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (timing and method)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' was sent by certified mail notifying Respondent of the Complaint and providing an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order must be sent (here: by certified mail) and must inform the respondent of the 40-day filing period and the specific regulatory grounds (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)) on which to base opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to respond (default determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and suspension is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent does not timely file a response contesting the imposition of reciprocal discipline, the USPTO may conclude there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose discipline identical to the state sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and duration of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO for three (3) years, commencing on the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies the practice areas covered (patent, trademark, other non-patent matters) and a definite suspension period (three years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required publication in the Official Gazette (content of Notice of Suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette: Notice of Suspension describing respondent, registration number, nature of violation, predicate state suspension, and summary of admitted misconduct and rules violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice should include: respondent's name and registration number; that reciprocal disciplinary proceeding resulted in a three-year suspension for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h); a summary of admitted misconduct (false billing statements, impermissible use of law firm resources, failure to timely provide documents/fees causing delays and abandonment, commingling client funds, not placing unearned fees in trust); the Utah Rules violated (1.3, 1.15(a) and (c), 8.4(c)); statutory basis (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24); and reference to the OED FOIA Reading Room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO must communicate the discipline and its reasons to relevant state disciplinary bodies, courts of admission, and the public per § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's post-discipline duties (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although specific duties are not reproduced in this Order, the respondent is required to follow the obligations set out in § 11.58 (e.g., client notification, file transfer, trust account handling) as applicable while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO action includes technical and administrative steps to remove the practitioner's association with Customer Numbers and PKI credentials to effectuate the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition prevents the suspended practitioner from using USPTO electronic filing/customer mechanisms until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of misconduct warranting discipline (admitted misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent admitted: submitting false billing statements to a law firm he had relationships with; impermissibly using resources of that law firm to provide legal services to his own clients; failing to timely provide documents and fees to properly respond to the USPTO in at least seven patent applications for six clients resulting in delays and one abandonment; comingling client funds with his own funds and not placing unearned fees in his trust account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific misconduct facts were set out in the Consent Agreement and formed the basis for the state suspension and the USPTO's reciprocal discipline; they also identify violations of Utah Rules of Professional Conduct (1.3, 1.15(a) and (c), 8.4(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and public access to disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations to statutory/regulatory authority must appear in the Order and the USPTO makes disciplinary decisions available publicly via the OED FOIA Reading Room.
